messages.Why you take it: Aciclovir treats herpes and shingles infections.
messages.How to take it: Start as early as possible and finish the course. Drink plenty of water.
messages.What to watch for: See a doctor if the rash involves the eye or you feel very unwell.

messages.Why you take it: Adrenaline injection treats severe allergic reactions in an emergency.
messages.How to take it: If you carry an auto-injector, inject into the outer thigh at the first sign of a severe reaction.
messages.What to watch for: Always go to hospital after using it, even if you feel better.

messages.Why you take it: Albendazole treats worm infections.
messages.How to take it: Take with food as a single dose or short course. Wash hands and cut nails short.
messages.What to watch for: See a doctor if tummy pain or worms persist.

messages.Why you take it: Amlodipine relaxes blood vessels to lower blood pressure and prevent stroke and heart attack.
messages.How to take it: Take once daily at the same time. It works gradually over 1-2 weeks.
messages.What to watch for: Ankle swelling and flushing can occur. Tell your doctor if swelling is troublesome.

messages.Why you take it: Amoxicillin is an antibiotic that treats bacterial infection.
messages.How to take it: Finish the whole course even when you feel better. Take at even intervals.
messages.What to watch for: Seek help for rash, swelling, severe diarrhoea or if you are not improving in 3 days.

messages.Why you take it: Low-dose aspirin makes blood less sticky, preventing heart attack and stroke.
messages.How to take it: Take once daily after food. Do not stop before surgery without advice.
messages.What to watch for: Seek help for black stools, vomiting blood or easy bruising.

messages.Why you take it: Atenolol slows the heart and lowers blood pressure, protecting the heart in angina or after attack.
messages.How to take it: Take at the same time daily. Never stop suddenly - this can trigger chest pain.
messages.What to watch for: Tell your doctor if your pulse is under 50, you feel faint, wheezy or very tired.

messages.Why you take it: Azithromycin is an antibiotic that treats bacterial infection.
messages.How to take it: Finish the whole course even when you feel better. Take at even intervals.
messages.What to watch for: Seek help for rash, swelling, severe diarrhoea or if you are not improving in 3 days.

messages.Why you take it: Betamethasone cream calms inflamed skin conditions such as eczema.
messages.How to take it: Apply thinly once or twice daily to affected skin only, for short periods.
messages.What to watch for: Do not use on the face for long. Tell your doctor if the skin thins.

messages.Why you take it: Bisoprolol slows the heart and lowers pressure. It helps in heart failure and after a heart attack.
messages.How to take it: Take once daily in the morning. Never stop suddenly.
messages.What to watch for: Tell your doctor if your pulse is under 50, you feel faint, wheezy or your ankles swell.

messages.Why you take it: Budesonide inhaler calms airway inflammation and prevents asthma attacks.
messages.How to take it: Use every day, even when well. Rinse your mouth after each use.
messages.What to watch for: Tell your doctor about a hoarse voice or white patches in the mouth.

messages.Why you take it: Canagliflozin removes sugar through urine. It also protects your heart and kidneys.
messages.How to take it: Take once daily before breakfast. Drink enough water and keep the genital area clean.
messages.What to watch for: Stop and seek help if vomiting, unable to eat, or with tummy pain and fast breathing.

messages.Why you take it: Candesartan lowers blood pressure and protects your kidneys and heart. It rarely causes cough.
messages.How to take it: Take at the same time daily, with or without food. Do not stop without advice.
messages.What to watch for: Tell your doctor if dizzy on standing. Pause and call the clinic if vomiting or dehydrated.

messages.Why you take it: Captopril lowers blood pressure and protects your heart and kidneys, especially in diabetes.
messages.How to take it: Take at the same time daily. Stand up slowly at first. Do not stop without advice.
messages.What to watch for: A dry cough is common - tell your doctor. Seek urgent help for lip or tongue swelling.

messages.Why you take it: Carvedilol protects a weakened heart and lowers blood pressure.
messages.How to take it: Take with food twice daily. Doses are increased slowly. Never stop suddenly.
messages.What to watch for: Dizziness is common at first. Tell your doctor if faint, wheezy or gaining weight fast.

messages.Why you take it: Cefaclor is an antibiotic that treats bacterial infection.
messages.How to take it: Finish the whole course even when you feel better. Take at even intervals.
messages.What to watch for: Seek help for rash, swelling, severe diarrhoea or if you are not improving in 3 days.

messages.Why you take it: Ceftriaxone is an antibiotic that treats bacterial infection.
messages.How to take it: Finish the whole course even when you feel better. Take at even intervals. Given by injection.
messages.What to watch for: Seek help for rash, swelling, severe diarrhoea or if you are not improving in 3 days.

messages.Why you take it: Cefuroxime is an antibiotic that treats bacterial infection.
messages.How to take it: Finish the whole course even when you feel better. Take at even intervals. Take with food.
messages.What to watch for: Seek help for rash, swelling, severe diarrhoea or if you are not improving in 3 days.

messages.Why you take it: Celecoxib reduces pain and inflammation with less stomach upset than other anti-inflammatories.
messages.How to take it: Take with food, lowest dose, shortest time.
messages.What to watch for: Avoid with heart disease or kidney disease. Seek help for chest pain or black stools.

messages.Why you take it: Chloroquine treats or prevents malaria.
messages.How to take it: Take with food exactly as prescribed.
messages.What to watch for: Tell your doctor about vision changes or itching.

messages.Why you take it: Chlorthalidone removes extra salt and water, lowering blood pressure for a full day.
messages.How to take it: Take once in the morning. Keep drinking normally.
messages.What to watch for: Tell your doctor if you have cramps, dizziness or gout pain. Blood tests check your salts.

messages.Why you take it: Ciprofloxacin is an antibiotic that treats bacterial infection.
messages.How to take it: Finish the whole course even when you feel better. Take at even intervals. Avoid milk and antacids a
messages.What to watch for: Seek help for rash, swelling, severe diarrhoea or if you are not improving in 3 days.

messages.Why you take it: Clarithromycin is an antibiotic that treats bacterial infection.
messages.How to take it: Finish the whole course even when you feel better. Take at even intervals.
messages.What to watch for: Seek help for rash, swelling, severe diarrhoea or if you are not improving in 3 days.

messages.Why you take it: Cloxacillin is an antibiotic that treats bacterial infection.
messages.How to take it: Finish the whole course even when you feel better. Take at even intervals. Take on an empty stomach.
messages.What to watch for: Seek help for rash, swelling, severe diarrhoea or if you are not improving in 3 days.

messages.Why you take it: Co-amoxiclav is an antibiotic that treats bacterial infection.
messages.How to take it: Finish the whole course even when you feel better. Take at even intervals. Take with food.
messages.What to watch for: Seek help for rash, swelling, severe diarrhoea or if you are not improving in 3 days.

messages.Why you take it: Co-trimoxazole is an antibiotic that treats bacterial infection.
messages.How to take it: Finish the whole course even when you feel better. Take at even intervals. Drink plenty of water.
messages.What to watch for: Seek help for rash, swelling, severe diarrhoea or if you are not improving in 3 days.

messages.Why you take it: Dexamethasone is a strong anti-inflammatory steroid given for short courses.
messages.How to take it: Take with food in the morning as prescribed.
messages.What to watch for: It can raise blood sugar and pressure. Check sugars more often if diabetic.

messages.Why you take it: Diazepam relieves severe anxiety or muscle spasm for a short time.
messages.How to take it: Use only as prescribed, for the shortest time. Do not drive or drink alcohol.
messages.What to watch for: It causes dependence with regular use. Do not stop suddenly after long use.

messages.Why you take it: Diclofenac reduces pain and inflammation. Use it only short-term.
messages.How to take it: Take with food for the shortest time possible.
messages.What to watch for: Avoid if you have kidney, heart or ulcer problems. Seek help for black stools or chest pain.

messages.Why you take it: Diltiazem lowers blood pressure and slows the heart, easing angina.
messages.How to take it: Take as prescribed; swallow slow-release capsules whole. Avoid grapefruit.
messages.What to watch for: Tell your doctor if your pulse is under 50, or you feel faint or breathless.

messages.Why you take it: Diphenhydramine eases allergy symptoms like itching, sneezing and hives.
messages.How to take it: Take as prescribed, usually at night as it causes drowsiness.
messages.What to watch for: Do not drive if drowsy.

messages.Why you take it: Doxycycline is an antibiotic that treats bacterial infection.
messages.How to take it: Finish the whole course even when you feel better. Take at even intervals. Take with a full glass of
messages.What to watch for: Seek help for rash, swelling, severe diarrhoea or if you are not improving in 3 days.

messages.Why you take it: Empagliflozin removes sugar through urine. It also protects your heart and kidneys.
messages.How to take it: Take once daily in the morning. Drink enough water and keep the genital area clean.
messages.What to watch for: Stop and seek help if vomiting, unable to eat, or with tummy pain and fast breathing.

messages.Why you take it: Enalapril lowers blood pressure and protects your heart and kidneys, especially in diabetes.
messages.How to take it: Take at the same time daily. Stand up slowly at first. Do not stop without advice.
messages.What to watch for: A dry cough is common - tell your doctor. Seek urgent help for lip or tongue swelling.

messages.Why you take it: Erythromycin is an antibiotic that treats bacterial infection.
messages.How to take it: Finish the whole course even when you feel better. Take at even intervals. Take with food.
messages.What to watch for: Seek help for rash, swelling, severe diarrhoea or if you are not improving in 3 days.

messages.Why you take it: Esomeprazole reduces stomach acid, healing ulcers and easing reflux. It also protects from aspirin.
messages.How to take it: Take 30 minutes before breakfast. Use for the shortest time needed.
messages.What to watch for: Long-term use can lower magnesium and B12. Tell your doctor if you need it for over 3 months.

messages.Why you take it: Famotidine reduces stomach acid to ease heartburn and heal ulcers.
messages.How to take it: Take once or twice daily as prescribed, or at bedtime for night symptoms.
messages.What to watch for: See a doctor if symptoms last over 2 weeks or you have black stools.

messages.Why you take it: Fexofenadine eases allergy symptoms like itching, sneezing and hives.
messages.How to take it: Take once daily.
messages.What to watch for: Rarely causes drowsiness. See a doctor if swelling or wheeze develops.

messages.Why you take it: Fluconazole treats fungal infections such as thrush.
messages.How to take it: Take as prescribed - often a single dose or a short course.
messages.What to watch for: Tell your doctor if you have liver problems or notice yellow eyes.

messages.Why you take it: Furosemide (Lasix) removes fluid, easing swelling and breathlessness in heart or kidney disease.
messages.How to take it: Take in the morning. If twice daily, take the second dose by mid-afternoon.
messages.What to watch for: Tell your doctor if dizzy, cramping, or passing very little urine. Pause if vomiting and call.

messages.Why you take it: Gabapentin eases nerve pain, such as burning feet from diabetes.
messages.How to take it: Doses are increased slowly. Do not stop suddenly. Avoid driving until you know how it affects you.
messages.What to watch for: Tell your doctor about drowsiness, dizziness, swelling or low mood.

messages.Why you take it: Gentamicin drops treat eye or ear infection.
messages.How to take it: Use as prescribed and finish the course. Do not share the bottle.
messages.What to watch for: See a doctor if pain, discharge or vision worsens.

messages.Why you take it: Glibenclamide helps your body release more insulin, lowering blood sugar.
messages.How to take it: Take with breakfast and never skip meals. Avoid alcohol on an empty stomach.
messages.What to watch for: Low sugar can last long with this tablet. Treat sweating or shaking with sugar and tell your doctor.

messages.Why you take it: Gliclazide helps your body release more insulin, lowering blood sugar.
messages.How to take it: Take before breakfast (and dinner if twice daily). Never skip meals after taking it.
messages.What to watch for: Low sugar signs: sweating, shaking, hunger. Take sugar or a sweet drink at once, then eat.

messages.Why you take it: Glimepiride helps your body release more insulin, lowering blood sugar.
messages.How to take it: Take once daily with breakfast. Never skip the meal after taking it.
messages.What to watch for: Low sugar signs: sweating, shaking, hunger. Take sugar or a sweet drink at once, then eat.

messages.Why you take it: Glipizide helps your body release more insulin, lowering blood sugar.
messages.How to take it: Take 30 minutes before a meal. Do not skip meals after taking it.
messages.What to watch for: Low sugar signs: sweating, shaking, hunger. Take sugar or a sweet drink at once, then eat.

messages.Why you take it: Griseofulvin treats fungal infections of skin, hair and nails.
messages.How to take it: Take with fatty food and complete the full course, which may be weeks.
messages.What to watch for: Tell your doctor about rash, headache or upset stomach.

messages.Why you take it: Hydrochlorothiazide removes extra salt and water, lowering blood pressure.
messages.How to take it: Take in the morning so you are not up at night. Keep drinking normally.
messages.What to watch for: Tell your doctor if you have cramps, dizziness or gout pain. Blood tests check your salts.

messages.Why you take it: Hydrocortisone cream calms skin inflammation; the injection treats severe allergy or asthma.
messages.How to take it: Apply cream thinly once or twice daily for the shortest time.
messages.What to watch for: Tell your doctor if skin thins or the rash worsens.

messages.Why you take it: Hyoscine eases cramping tummy pain by relaxing gut muscle.
messages.How to take it: Take as prescribed when cramps occur.
messages.What to watch for: Tell your doctor about a dry mouth, blurred vision or difficulty passing urine.

messages.Why you take it: Ibuprofen reduces pain and inflammation. Use it only short-term.
messages.How to take it: Take with food. Use the lowest dose for the shortest time.
messages.What to watch for: Avoid if you have kidney disease, heart failure, high pressure or ulcers. Stop for black stools.

messages.Why you take it: Indapamide gently removes salt and water to lower blood pressure and prevent stroke.
messages.How to take it: Take once in the morning. Keep drinking normally.
messages.What to watch for: Tell your doctor if you have cramps, dizziness or gout pain. Blood tests check your salts.

messages.Why you take it: Insulin replaces what your body cannot make, keeping sugar safe for your eyes, kidneys and heart.
messages.How to take it: Inject as timed by your doctor, rotate sites and store unopened insulin in the fridge.
messages.What to watch for: Low sugar: sweating, shaking, confusion. Take sugar at once. Carry glucose sweets always.

messages.Why you take it: Insulin replaces what your body cannot make, keeping sugar safe for your eyes, kidneys and heart.
messages.How to take it: Inject at the same time every day, even if not eating. Rotate injection sites.
messages.What to watch for: Low sugar: sweating, shaking, confusion. Take sugar at once. Carry glucose sweets always.

messages.Why you take it: Insulin replaces what your body cannot make, keeping sugar safe for your eyes, kidneys and heart.
messages.How to take it: Inject just before eating. Rotate injection sites. Do not inject if you will not eat.
messages.What to watch for: Low sugar: sweating, shaking, confusion. Take sugar at once. Carry glucose sweets always.

messages.Why you take it: Insulin replaces what your body cannot make, keeping sugar safe for your eyes, kidneys and heart.
messages.How to take it: Inject 30 minutes before meals. Rotate sites on the tummy or thigh. Never skip the meal.
messages.What to watch for: Low sugar: sweating, shaking, confusion. Take sugar at once. Carry glucose sweets always.

messages.Why you take it: Irbesartan lowers blood pressure and protects your kidneys and heart. It rarely causes cough.
messages.How to take it: Take at the same time daily, with or without food. Do not stop without advice.
messages.What to watch for: Tell your doctor if dizzy on standing. Pause and call the clinic if vomiting or dehydrated.

messages.Why you take it: Ketoconazole treats fungal skin infections and dandruff.
messages.How to take it: Use shampoo, cream or soap as directed. Tablets are only for short courses.
messages.What to watch for: Stop tablets and see a doctor for yellow eyes, dark urine or tummy pain.

messages.Why you take it: Labetalol lowers blood pressure and is safe in pregnancy.
messages.How to take it: Take with food as prescribed. Never stop suddenly.
messages.What to watch for: Tell your doctor if faint on standing, wheezy or very tired.

messages.Why you take it: Levofloxacin is an antibiotic that treats bacterial infection.
messages.How to take it: Finish the whole course even when you feel better. Take at even intervals.
messages.What to watch for: Seek help for rash, swelling, severe diarrhoea or if you are not improving in 3 days.

messages.Why you take it: Levothyroxine replaces thyroid hormone, restoring energy and a normal metabolism.
messages.How to take it: Take every morning on an empty stomach, 30 minutes before food, tea or other tablets.
messages.What to watch for: Tell your doctor about palpitations, sweating or weight loss - the dose may be too high.

messages.Why you take it: Lisinopril lowers blood pressure and protects your heart and kidneys, especially in diabetes.
messages.How to take it: Take at the same time daily. Stand up slowly at first. Do not stop without advice.
messages.What to watch for: A dry cough is common - tell your doctor. Seek urgent help for lip or tongue swelling.

messages.Why you take it: Loratadine eases allergy symptoms like itching, sneezing and hives.
messages.How to take it: Take once daily.
messages.What to watch for: Rarely causes drowsiness. See a doctor if swelling or wheeze develops.

messages.Why you take it: Losartan lowers blood pressure and protects your kidneys and heart. It rarely causes cough.
messages.How to take it: Take at the same time daily, with or without food. Do not stop without advice.
messages.What to watch for: Tell your doctor if dizzy on standing. Pause and call the clinic if vomiting or dehydrated.

messages.Why you take it: Magnesium sulfate is given in hospital to prevent fits in severe pregnancy blood pressure.
messages.How to take it: It is given by drip or injection under nursing supervision.
messages.What to watch for: Tell staff at once if you feel very flushed, weak or breathless.

messages.Why you take it: Metformin lowers blood sugar and helps protect your heart. It does not cause low sugar on its own.
messages.How to take it: Take with or after food to avoid stomach upset. Do not stop it when unwell unless told to.
messages.What to watch for: Tell your doctor if you have vomiting or diarrhoea, or when a kidney test is due - dose may change.

messages.Why you take it: Metoclopramide eases nausea and helps the stomach empty.
messages.How to take it: Take before meals, for no more than 5 days.
messages.What to watch for: Stop and seek help for muscle spasms of the face or neck or restlessness.

messages.Why you take it: Metoprolol slows the heart and lowers blood pressure, protecting the heart.
messages.How to take it: Take with food at the same times daily. Never stop suddenly.
messages.What to watch for: Tell your doctor if your pulse is under 50, you feel faint, wheezy or very tired.

messages.Why you take it: Metronidazole gel treats skin conditions such as rosacea.
messages.How to take it: Apply thinly twice daily to clean skin.
messages.What to watch for: Stop and see a doctor if irritation worsens.

messages.Why you take it: Metronidazole is an antibiotic that treats bacterial infection.
messages.How to take it: Finish the whole course even when you feel better. Take at even intervals. No alcohol during and for
messages.What to watch for: Seek help for rash, swelling, severe diarrhoea or if you are not improving in 3 days.

messages.Why you take it: A multivitamin tops up vitamins when diet is limited or during pregnancy.
messages.How to take it: Take one daily with food.
messages.What to watch for: It does not replace a balanced diet. Keep out of reach of children.

messages.Why you take it: Neomycin cream treats minor skin infection.
messages.How to take it: Apply thinly to clean skin as prescribed.
messages.What to watch for: Stop and see a doctor if redness spreads or the skin becomes itchy.

messages.Why you take it: Nifedipine relaxes blood vessels to lower blood pressure.
messages.How to take it: Swallow slow-release tablets whole. Take at the same time daily.
messages.What to watch for: Tell your doctor about ankle swelling, headache or flushing that does not settle.

messages.Why you take it: Fluids through a drip replace lost water and salts or sugar.
messages.How to take it: Given in clinic or hospital.
messages.What to watch for: Tell staff if the drip site is painful or swollen.

messages.Why you take it: Nystatin treats thrush in the mouth or on skin.
messages.How to take it: Hold the liquid in the mouth before swallowing, after food, 4 times daily.
messages.What to watch for: See a doctor if not improving within a week.

messages.Why you take it: Olmesartan lowers blood pressure and protects your kidneys and heart. It rarely causes cough.
messages.How to take it: Take at the same time daily, with or without food. Do not stop without advice.
messages.What to watch for: Tell your doctor if dizzy on standing. Pause and call the clinic if vomiting or dehydrated.

messages.Why you take it: Omeprazole reduces stomach acid, healing ulcers and easing reflux. It also protects from aspirin.
messages.How to take it: Take 30 minutes before breakfast. Use for the shortest time needed.
messages.What to watch for: Long-term use can lower magnesium and B12. Tell your doctor if you need it for over 3 months.

messages.Why you take it: Ondansetron stops nausea and vomiting.
messages.How to take it: Take as prescribed, up to 3 times a day. Sip fluids often.
messages.What to watch for: See a doctor if vomiting continues over 24 hours or you cannot keep fluids down.

messages.Why you take it: Oxycodone is a strong painkiller for severe pain, used under close supervision.
messages.How to take it: Take exactly as prescribed. Do not drive, drink alcohol or share it.
messages.What to watch for: Seek urgent help for very slow breathing or extreme drowsiness. It can cause dependence.

messages.Why you take it: Pantoprazole reduces stomach acid, healing ulcers and easing reflux. It also protects from aspirin.
messages.How to take it: Take 30 minutes before breakfast. Use for the shortest time needed.
messages.What to watch for: Long-term use can lower magnesium and B12. Tell your doctor if you need it for over 3 months.

messages.Why you take it: Paracetamol eases pain and fever and is safe with most other medicines.
messages.How to take it: Adults: up to 1 g every 4-6 hours, maximum 4 g a day. Check other products for hidden paracetamol.
messages.What to watch for: Never exceed the daily limit - overdose harms the liver. Seek help if you have taken too much.

messages.Why you take it: Perindopril lowers blood pressure and protects your heart and kidneys, especially in diabetes.
messages.How to take it: Take at the same time daily. Stand up slowly at first. Do not stop without advice.
messages.What to watch for: A dry cough is common - tell your doctor. Seek urgent help for lip or tongue swelling.

messages.Why you take it: Pioglitazone helps your body respond to insulin, lowering blood sugar over weeks.
messages.How to take it: Take once daily at the same time, with or without food.
messages.What to watch for: Tell your doctor about ankle swelling, breathlessness or rapid weight gain.

messages.Why you take it: Prednisone calms inflammation in conditions like asthma flares or allergy.
messages.How to take it: Take in the morning with food. Do not stop a long course suddenly.
messages.What to watch for: It can raise blood sugar and pressure. Check sugars more often if diabetic.

messages.Why you take it: Primaquine clears malaria parasites from the liver to prevent relapse.
messages.How to take it: Take with food and complete the full course.
messages.What to watch for: Seek help for dark urine or yellow eyes.

messages.Why you take it: Propranolol slows the heart and lowers pressure. It also eases tremor, migraine and anxiety.
messages.How to take it: Take as prescribed. Never stop suddenly.
messages.What to watch for: Tell your doctor if wheezy, very tired, or your pulse is under 50. Avoid if you have asthma.

messages.Why you take it: Ramipril lowers blood pressure and protects your heart and kidneys, especially in diabetes.
messages.How to take it: Take at the same time daily. Stand up slowly at first. Do not stop without advice.
messages.What to watch for: A dry cough is common - tell your doctor. Seek urgent help for lip or tongue swelling.

messages.Why you take it: Ranitidine reduces stomach acid to ease heartburn and heal ulcers.
messages.How to take it: Take as prescribed, usually at night or twice daily.
messages.What to watch for: See a doctor if symptoms last over 2 weeks or you have black stools.

messages.Why you take it: Rosiglitazone helps your body respond to insulin, lowering blood sugar over weeks.
messages.How to take it: Take once or twice daily at the same times.
messages.What to watch for: Tell your doctor about ankle swelling, breathlessness or rapid weight gain.

messages.Why you take it: Salbutamol opens the airways quickly to relieve wheeze and breathlessness.
messages.How to take it: Use when needed. If needed more than 3 times a week, your preventer needs review.
messages.What to watch for: Seek urgent help if it is not working or you cannot speak in full sentences.

messages.Why you take it: Simvastatin lowers cholesterol and protects the heart and brain, even when cholesterol seems normal.
messages.How to take it: Take at night. Avoid grapefruit juice. Keep taking it - it works over months.
messages.What to watch for: Tell your doctor about unexplained muscle pain or dark urine.

messages.Why you take it: Telmisartan lowers blood pressure and protects your kidneys and heart. It rarely causes cough.
messages.How to take it: Take at the same time daily, with or without food. Do not stop without advice.
messages.What to watch for: Tell your doctor if dizzy on standing. Pause and call the clinic if vomiting or dehydrated.

messages.Why you take it: Tetracycline is an antibiotic that treats bacterial infection.
messages.How to take it: Finish the whole course even when you feel better. Take at even intervals. Take on an empty stomach;
messages.What to watch for: Seek help for rash, swelling, severe diarrhoea or if you are not improving in 3 days.

messages.Why you take it: Tiotropium keeps the airways open for 24 hours in COPD.
messages.How to take it: Use once daily at the same time. It is not for sudden attacks - use your reliever for those.
messages.What to watch for: Tell your doctor about a dry mouth or difficulty passing urine.

messages.Why you take it: Tolbutamide helps your body release more insulin, lowering blood sugar.
messages.How to take it: Take with meals as prescribed and do not skip meals.
messages.What to watch for: Low sugar signs: sweating, shaking, hunger. Take sugar or a sweet drink at once, then eat.

messages.Why you take it: Tolnaftate cream treats athlete's foot and ringworm.
messages.How to take it: Apply twice daily to clean, dry skin for 2-4 weeks.
messages.What to watch for: See a doctor if it spreads or does not clear.

messages.Why you take it: Tramadol is a strong painkiller for short-term moderate pain.
messages.How to take it: Take only as prescribed. Do not drive if drowsy. Do not drink alcohol.
messages.What to watch for: It can cause dependence, nausea and drowsiness. Do not take with other sleepy medicines.

messages.Why you take it: Valsartan lowers blood pressure and protects your kidneys and heart. It rarely causes cough.
messages.How to take it: Take at the same time daily, with or without food. Do not stop without advice.
messages.What to watch for: Tell your doctor if dizzy on standing. Pause and call the clinic if vomiting or dehydrated.

messages.Why you take it: Verapamil lowers blood pressure and controls heart rhythm.
messages.How to take it: Take as prescribed with food. Avoid grapefruit juice.
messages.What to watch for: Constipation is common. Tell your doctor if your pulse is under 50 or you feel faint.

messages.Why you take it: Vitamin B12 is needed for healthy blood and nerves. Metformin can lower it.
messages.How to take it: Take as prescribed, or attend for injections.
messages.What to watch for: Tell your doctor about numbness or tingling in the feet.

messages.Why you take it: Vitamin C supports healing and helps absorb iron.
messages.How to take it: Take with meals, especially with iron tablets.
messages.What to watch for: High doses can cause stomach upset or kidney stones.
